page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.6xlarge is a storage-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is powered by an arm64 architecture utilizing 24 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family running at 2.8 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core. Hardware caching is configured with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. The instance is provisioned with 192 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per core ratio. Network connectivity is supported by a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while graphics accelerators are omitted.

Storage configuration is defined by 15,000 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, bypassing network attached storage latency for high-throughput disk workloads. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier execution in database operations and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, which reaches 378.34 GB/s. Memory write speeds and Geekbench multi-core scoring place in the top quartile, alongside solid results in compilation and static web serving throughput exceeding 56 GB/s. Standard integer and cryptographic execution deliver average results matching its 24-core allocation.

The absence of dedicated GPU hardware limits the instance in machine learning inference, where small and large language model generation scores fall into lower performance brackets. Similarly, single-core execution metrics are modest compared to high-frequency x86 compute instances. However, the high density of local NVMe storage combined with a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides a resource profile balanced toward disk-bound throughput and memory-resident lookups.

The i8ge.6xlarge is tailored for input/output intensive applications that require high NVMe capacity directly connected to the host. Best-fit workloads include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing engines, extract-transform-load pipelines, and high-capacity caching nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.6xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 24 dedicated arm64 physical cores using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz, with 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 192 GB, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio that records top-tier results in uncached read bandwidth at 378.34 GB/s and memory benchmarks. A critical asset is the bundled 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD array, which eliminates network storage latency and directly underpins top-tier benchmark throughput in database operations. Network performance is anchored by a 38 Gbps baseline. Without hardware accelerators, text generation and LLM processing remain low, reflecting its focus on local I/O rather than machine learning inference. The i8ge.6xlarge represents an efficient allocation of high-density storage and substantial memory, making it well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, caching tiers, and large-scale analytical processing.
